forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

summary.summary: Maldon is a small, low-debt authority: it held no external long-term debt in 2025/26 bar a five-year hire-purchase agreement for two tractors, and is internally under-borrowed by £8.552m rather than exposed to market refinancing. Investments held fell by £3m over the year to £16.4m at 31 March 2026, but investment income comfortably beat budget: £1.047m actual against £0.664m budgeted, at an average return of 4.6%. The Section 151 Officer reports full compliance with every prudential indicator and the approved Treasury Management Strategy for the year, and there is no distress language anywhere in the report.

signals.headline: No external long-term debt other than a small tractor hire-purchase agreement; all Prudential Indicators complied with throughout 2025/26; investment income £1.047m actual vs £0.664m budget
signals.why: Verified quiet — a well-funded, effectively debt-free position with outturn income ahead of budget.

news_drafts.headline: Maldon auditors say its minimum revenue provision policy does not fully reflect its internal borrowing
news_drafts.lead:
Maldon District Council's external auditors have reported that its policy on minimum revenue provision, the amount it must set aside from each year's budget to pay off past borrowing, does not fully reflect its use of internal borrowing. Internal borrowing means paying for capital spending from the council's own cash reserves instead of taking a loan. The finding is in the auditors' interim annual report, item 7B for the Performance, Governance and Audit Committee on 12 November 2026.

The paper says the policy does not match the council's current capital financing arrangements. It says "the level of internal borrowing is expected to increase", and it links that expected increase to planned investment in leisure centres.

The paper gives no figures for the amount of internal borrowing or for the provision the council makes.

news_drafts.headline: Maldon plans to use £3.2m of its own cash to fund 45% of its £7.1m capital programme
news_drafts.lead:
Maldon District Council plans to pay for £3.2m of its £7.1m capital programme by internal borrowing, according to an appendix to the Strategy and Resources Committee papers for 24 September 2026. Capital spending is money spent on things that last, such as buildings, roads, vehicles and equipment. Internal borrowing means using the council's own cash reserves to pay for that spending instead of taking out a loan, which saves interest but uses up the cushion. The £3.2m is 45% of total capital funding of £7,054,000.

The appendix lists the £3.2m as the same figure in both of the columns shown, with no change between them, and attributes it to the general fund, the council's main account for day-to-day services. The papers describe it as the largest single funding source after general reserves, which are money set aside as a cushion for the unexpected.

The papers state that the internal borrowing will require repayment in future and affects the council's liquidity position, meaning the cash it has available at any time. They do not set out in the material reviewed here when the money would be paid back or how.

news_drafts.headline: Maldon faces audit recovery after three years without account sign-off
news_drafts.lead: The council's accounts have not received auditor sign-off for more than three years, because the balance sheet position could not be fully verified. External auditors have issued disclaimed opinions for this entire period — meaning they were unable to form any opinion on whether the accounts are correct. The auditors have now assessed the council as 'B' rated under the government's rebuild framework, with recovery targeted by November 2027. The council must fully reconcile its balance sheet across the six-year period from March 2021 through March 2027 to enable auditors to sign off the accounts once more.

findings.headline: Auditors find that some Maldon District Council policies had not been reviewed for several years, with review dates and version records not consistently documented
findings.detail: The auditors recommended a standardised policy management approach with defined review cycles and a central register. The related prior-year recommendation had not been fully addressed.
findings.matters: A repeated governance recommendation that remains open is a point a peer council reviewing its own policy controls would look for.
findings.quote: had not been reviewed for several years

findings.headline: Auditors identify that Maldon District Council has no formal process to review, monitor or approve tender waivers
findings.detail: The paper says the absence of a formal approval and monitoring framework may reduce transparency and weaken governance over procurement decisions. The auditors have raised a performance improvement observation.
findings.matters: Procurement waivers without a formal approval process are a control gap that other councils can check in their own contract rules.
findings.quote: the Council does not have a formal process in place to review, monitor, or approve tender waivers

findings.headline: Auditors have not yet concluded on the 2025/26 financial statements, because the Auditor's Annual Report was issued before audit work on the accounts was complete
findings.detail: The paper says the Code of Audit Practice requires the report by 30 November, so it was issued before audit work on the financial statements and other information was finished. The auditors have not reached their conclusions on those areas.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender relying on the annual report should know that the opinion on the accounts is still outstanding.
findings.quote: we have not reached our conclusions in respect of these areas

findings.headline: Maldon District Council's share of the Essex local government reorganisation programme costs is expected to be about £26,000 out of £78,000 in total
findings.detail: The paper says the programme entered organised closure after the government paused it in September 2026. The council's share is subject to final confirmation, and management judged the cost not significant to the overall financial position.
findings.matters: Reorganisation spending that is written off after a government pause is a cost other councils in the same position will face, and the final allocation is still open.
findings.figures: £78,000 estimated programme costs; approximately £26,000 Maldon share
findings.quote: with Maldon District Council's share expected to be approximately £26,000, subject to final confirmation

findings.headline: Auditors say Maldon District Council's Minimum Revenue Provision policy does not fully reflect its use of internal borrowing, which is expected to increase
findings.detail: The paper says the policy does not match the council's current capital financing arrangements. It links the expected increase in internal borrowing to planned leisure centre investment.
findings.matters: Internal borrowing that is not reflected in the MRP policy understates the revenue cost of capital spending, a point finance directors check when reviewing their own MRP.
findings.quote: the level of internal borrowing is expected to increase
